approach: Fix in detail_from_job_logs (crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs:248, tail built at 293-294), where the stored tail is built. Add two small pure helpers beside tail_lines in checks.rs: `without_post_job_cleanup(log)` cuts a CI job log at its first runner post-job marker line, and `failure_tail(text, n)` tails the text but, when that tail has no failure evidence (`test result`, `FAILED`, `failures:`, `panicked at`) and the text does, returns the evidence lines with 2 lines of context each, under the same line and byte caps. detail_from_job_logs cuts the cleanup from each readable log before assembling `text` and uses `failure_tail` instead of `tail_lines`. Name parsing, the FAILING_UNITS_PREFIX header, redaction and the local check tail (checks.rs:533) are unchanged. Add tests in gh/tests.rs (through detail_from_job_logs) and checks.rs (helpers), and a CHANGELOG Fixed entry naming the root cause. Criterion 5 is answered with an explicit seam and fails_without: the three CI commands run the new tests, so they exit non-zero on the base commit.

decisions.choice: Fix in detail_from_job_logs, using helpers in checks.rs next to tail_lines.
decisions.reason: The fault is that the whole job log, which ends with runner cleanup, is tailed and failure lines are never selected. CiSource::failure_detail (gh/client.rs ~998-1025) is the only non-test caller, so every CI-reused failed check goes through the fix.

rejected.why: It receives a tail already cut at 200 lines, so the failure lines may already be lost; it also serves the routing path where the detail is a fake.

rejected.option: Parse failing test output only and drop the tail
rejected.why: failed_test_names already does this and yields nothing for an unfinished shard or non-cargo output, which is the case that showed noise.

rejected.option: Change the local failed-check tail at checks.rs:533
rejected.why: Local output is the command's own output with no runner cleanup; out of scope.

decisions.choice: Cut at the first line whose trimmed text is exactly `Post job cleanup.` or `Cleaning up orphan processes`, or starts with `##[group]Post `; keep the original log if the cut would leave only whitespace.
decisions.reason: These are the runner's markers for the post-job phase; whole-line anchoring stops test output matching by accident, and the guard keeps a log that starts with a marker readable.

rejected.why: A noise filter list grows without end and can drop real output; cutting the trailing phase is bounded.

decisions.choice: Fall back to evidence lines only when the plain tail has none of the four evidence strings and the log has some; otherwise keep the plain tail.
decisions.reason: Logs with evidence in the tail, or none at all, behave as before, so the existing tests keep passing.

rejected.why: It would drop surrounding assertion output and change existing tail contents.

decisions.choice: For criterion 5, no new test code; the demonstration is the three CI commands, whose test run includes the new tests.
decisions.reason: The new behavior tests make `cargo test --locked` red on the base commit, so the command shows the fix, not only a green build.

rejected.option: Add a separate meta-test that runs cargo
rejected.why: It would add logic with no gain; the new tests already exercise detail_from_job_logs.

files.purpose: Add FAILURE_EVIDENCE, without_post_job_cleanup and failure_tail beside tail_lines (~line 193), with doc comments naming the root cause, plus unit tests.
In detail_from_job_logs, cut cleanup from each readable log and build the tail with failure_tail; update the function doc (~238-247) to name the root cause.
Add the two detail_from_job_logs tests after job_log_parser_strips_stamps_keeps_the_indent_and_names_the_units.
Add a Fixed entry under Unreleased naming the root cause and the fix in detail_from_job_logs.

steps: In checks.rs, below tail_lines, add `const FAILURE_EVIDENCE: [&str; 4] = ["test result", "FAILED", "failures:", "panicked at"]` and `pub fn without_post_job_cleanup(log: &str) -> &str`: find the byte offset of the first line whose trim equals `Post job cleanup.` or `Cleaning up orphan processes` or starts with `##[group]Post `; return the text before it, or the whole log if no marker is found or the cut leaves only whitespace.

In checks.rs add `pub fn failure_tail(text: &str, n: usize) -> String`: let `plain = tail_lines(text, n)`; if `plain` has a line with any FAILURE_EVIDENCE string, or `text` has none, return `plain`; else collect each matching line of `text` with the 2 lines after it (no duplicates, in order), join with newlines and a final newline, and return `tail_lines(.., n)`. Doc comment names the root cause.

In gh/client.rs detail_from_job_logs, in the `readable` loop push `without_post_job_cleanup(log)` instead of the full log, and replace `tail_lines(&text, FAILED_TAIL_LINES)` (line 293) with `failure_tail(&text, FAILED_TAIL_LINES)`, keeping the `tail(.., FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)` cap (line 294). Leave the names/units code on the full plain log. Update the function doc.

In gh/tests.rs add `detail_from_job_logs_drops_the_post_job_cleanup_tail` and `detail_from_job_logs_keeps_failure_lines_when_no_test_is_named`, built with `stamped`, each asserting the content of output_tail as in the demonstrations.

In checks.rs tests add unit tests for `without_post_job_cleanup` (cut at each marker, no marker unchanged, marker first line keeps the log) and `failure_tail` (no evidence returns the plain tail; evidence only outside the last n lines is returned; the n cap holds).
Add a bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed` in CHANGELOG.md naming the root cause and the fix in detail_from_job_logs.
Run cargo fmt --all, then `cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked`, and fix any failure.

risks.risk: A post-job marker string appears earlier in a log (for example a Post step of an action before the tests) and the cut removes test output.
risks.mitigation: Match whole trimmed lines only; keep the uncut log if the cut leaves nothing; failed_test_names still runs on the full plain log, so names are never lost by the cut.

risks.risk: The evidence-line fallback keeps too little context for an assertion.
risks.mitigation: Keep 2 lines after each match, remove overlaps, and apply it only when the plain tail has no evidence.

risks.risk: The fallback fires on a tail that has no evidence even though the failure is in a non-cargo tool.
risks.mitigation: If the log has no evidence lines, failure_tail returns the plain tail, so behavior changes only when evidence exists elsewhere.

demonstrations.method: New test `detail_from_job_logs_drops_the_post_job_cleanup_tail` in gh/tests.rs. It builds a log with the existing `stamped` helper (gh/tests.rs ~376): a failing cargo section (`Running`, `failures:`, a `panicked at` line, `test ... FAILED`, `test result: FAILED`), then `Post job cleanup.`, `[command]/usr/bin/git config --local --unset-all ...`, `Cleaning up orphan processes` and a `##[warning]Node.js 20 actions are deprecated` line. It calls the production `detail_from_job_logs(name, "failure", Some(log))` and asserts on the returned detail. The log is real input; nothing is faked.
demonstrations.observes: output_tail contains `panicked at` and `FAILED` and none of `Post job cleanup`, `unset-all`, `Cleaning up orphan processes`, `Node.js`; failed_tests names the test.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base commit the tail is the last 200 lines of the whole log, so the cleanup text is present and the not-contains assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point detail_from_job_logs (pub, gh/client.rs:248); the input is a log string built by the `stamped` helper (exists); no double. The test function is added in plan step 4.

demonstrations.method: New test `detail_from_job_logs_keeps_failure_lines_when_no_test_is_named` in gh/tests.rs. The log has no `Running` or `Doc-tests` line, so failed_test_names yields no names: a `thread 'x' panicked at` line with an assertion message, `test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed`, `failures:`; then 250 progress lines (`compiling crate_N`, no evidence strings) and the cleanup block. Conclusion `cancelled`. It calls detail_from_job_logs.
demonstrations.observes: failed_tests is empty; output_tail contains `panicked at`, the assertion text, `test result: FAILED` and `failures:`, and no cleanup text.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base commit the last 200 lines are only progress lines plus cleanup, so the `panicked at` / `test result` assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point detail_from_job_logs (gh/client.rs:248) with the existing `stamped` helper (exists); no double; test added in plan step 4.

demonstrations.method: Existing checks tests run unchanged (tail_lines at checks.rs:755-758, the 200-line cap at ~639 and ~762, the byte cap at ~783, FAILING_UNITS_PREFIX and redaction tests in gh/tests.rs). New checks.rs unit tests call the pure helpers directly: `without_post_job_cleanup` (no marker returns the text unchanged; a marker on the first line keeps the log; each marker cuts) and `failure_tail` (a log with no evidence strings returns exactly what `tail_lines` returns; the n cap holds; evidence outside the last n lines is returned). The gh test `reused_red_degrades_when_the_log_lists_no_failures` covers a no-evidence, no-cleanup log through detail_from_job_logs.
demonstrations.observes: All checks tests pass, including the existing tail and cap tests and the new plain-tail equality tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: If failure_tail or the cut altered ordinary logs, the plain-tail equality tests and the existing cap tests would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Pure functions `without_post_job_cleanup` and `failure_tail` in checks.rs, called directly with string inputs; no double. The helpers are added in plan steps 1-2 and their tests in step 5; tail_lines, tail and the existing tests exist today.
